0.q: E. coli KNabc (pUC19–HaNhaD) and E. coli KNabc (pUC19–HaMrpD) exhibited enhanced Na+ tolerance in the presence of 100–500 mM NaCl, indicating that these two antiporters are mainly responsible for Na+/H+ exchange.

1.q: The expression of HaNhaP and HaPhaD resulted in weak growth of recombinant E. coli TK2420, compared with the control, at low potassium concentrations (0–40 mM), which implied that HaNhaP and HaPhaD were capable of exporting K+.
